report:
Reviewed meta.reviews.selector_whole_file independently against its current complete claim, its single ordinary implementation association in sage_meta::review (lib:sage_meta), and its complete associated ordinary test set: sage_meta::whole_files_and_ranges_preserve_exact_line_endings_and_detect_selected_edits (test:review). There are no TODO or N/A entries.

The requirements are selection of all source-file contents, preservation of any trailing newline, and absence of additional selector payload. The implementation's Selector::WholeFile unit variant carries no fields. select resolves the source path and returns std::fs::read_to_string(resolved) directly, without trimming, line splitting, or newline normalization. capture_read saves that same returned text through source_lines, which splits on newline while retaining terminal empty elements; joining the saved elements reconstructs the text. input_errors reselects captured reads and compares exact reconstructed strings, so a newly added terminal newline is significant. These operations and the data model are all in the initially captured review.rs; no additional production implementation association is necessary.

The associated test uses a concrete fixture file with CRLF, a blank line, LF, and a final unterminated line. Its two whole-file calls assert exact equality to the full input, and it asserts equality of repeated captured fragments and exact reconstruction of persisted contents. After recording, it appends only a final newline and asserts that checking becomes invalid. This tests both complete selection and the significance of the trailing newline, catching trimming or truncation implementations. Its preceding range assertions distinguish partial selection from the whole-file behavior and establish a valid baseline before selected-content changes invalidate the record. The fixture helper source was captured with review read (lines 1–108): writes use std::fs::write directly, input reads the persisted JSON, and start/record use the actual review APIs. The unit selector construction in the test together with the fieldless enum definition adequately accounts for no additional selector data; an isolated assertion of every serialized field is unnecessary for this claim. Empty files and files already ending in newlines follow the same unmodified read and reversible split path; the claim does not require separate per-input tests. The complete set gives meaningful assertions for the stated guarantee.

I read the review specification and required repository guidance and reassessed the evidence rather than inheriting a baseline verdict. Commands I executed were review start, recorded reads, and source/JSON inspection, followed by review record for this report. I did not rerun test suites or edit Rust. The coordinator now reports 331 sage-meta functional tests, 46 sage-stash tests, and workspace build passing; these are separately reported execution results, not commands executed by me. Source inspection found no claim violation or outstanding concern requiring reproduction. All claim aspects are accounted for; no edits requested.

Refresh assessment: compared every fresh initial fragment and association against the previously inspected input. The full claim and whole implementation file remain identical. The sole annotated test changes only by adding its meta.reviews.source_representation association; its complete executable body and assertions are unchanged and were reread. This additional association does not change whole-file semantics or reduce coverage. Recaptured the current fixture helpers for this new review; earlier snapshot equality was not used as a substitute for saving dependencies. Reassessed all three claim requirements against these current inputs and retained the source-specific reasoning above. No source files changed and no test commands were run during refresh.
